notes: Alaska daily/weekly overtime does not apply to employers of fewer than 4 employees; a DOL-approved flexible plan may use 10-hour days (DOL table).
No state meal-period requirement for adults in the DOL table; federal law does not require one.
No state paid rest-period requirement in the DOL table; federal law does not require one.
Drafted from US DOL WHD state tables (confidence=medium) on 2026-11-06; upgrade to primary sources pending.
minimum_wage.effective is the DOL table date (2026-11-05), not the statutory effective date.

Minors (AS 23.10.340): the 9 h daily cap counts school + work combined (school-day work cap not encodable without school hours); whether the 23 h weekly cap applies in vacation weeks is unclear, so it is encoded for school weeks only. Federal 3 h/18 h/7 p.m. limits (federal.json) also apply.
Minors (AS 23.10.350): under-18 may work at most 6 days a week and need a 30-minute break when scheduled 6+ consecutive hours (not encoded: no minor-break type).

rules.summary: Minors under 16 may work at most 23 hours a week outside school hours, with school plus work no more than 9 hours a day, between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m.

citation.title: AS 23.10.340 — Employment of children under 16
citation.excerpt: Employment outside school hours may not exceed 23 hours in one week, domestic work and baby-sitting excepted.

rules.summary: Minors under 16 may work at most 9 hours a day, between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m.

citation.title: AS 23.10.340 — Employment of children under 16
citation.excerpt: may not be employed for more than a combined total of nine hours school attendance and employment in one day. If employed, the minor's work may be performed only between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m.
